# Capstone 6: Modbus RTU interface and the host master: the exercise

<!-- Generated by tools/maintainer/build_exercise_readmes.py from the lesson page. Edit the lesson, then run the script. -->

Lessons: [Capstone 6: Modbus RTU interface and the host master](https://jouhis.github.io/embedded-course/lessons/0118-capstone-6-modbus-rtu-interface.html) and [Capstone 7: the bootloader and the image layout](https://jouhis.github.io/embedded-course/lessons/0119-capstone-7-the-bootloader-and.html). Read them first: the steps below refer to their diagrams and worked examples.

## Lesson 118: Try it: the register that starts the dryer

1. Build the starter firmware from the workspace root: `python -I tools/build.py projects/0118-dryer-modbus-bootloader/starter`. It should finish without errors. The one missing piece is a function body you have not written yet, and the build does not need it to link.
2. Open `projects/0118-dryer-modbus-bootloader/starter/app/regmap.c` and find the `TODO(learner)` comment in `regmap_publish()`. Write the seven registers that this function owns: the six read-only registers (SETPOINT_C, STATE, TEMP_X10, PWM_PCT, FAULT_CODE and REMAINING_MIN) and the MATERIAL register, which is copied so that a read shows the current material. The fields come from the state, the output and the temperature arguments, and the comment above the `TODO(learner)` marker gives each one. The temperature needs the cast from the section on two's complement.
3. Run the host test for the register map. It is the test project that lesson 120 explains, and you can run it now: `python -I tools/build.py projects/0120-dryer-host-tests/starter --clean --test`. Before your change, expect `90% tests passed, 1 tests failed out of 10`, with `10 - regmap (Failed)` in the list. After it, expect `100% tests passed out of 10`. Then build the firmware again, as in step 1.
4. Optional, with `pyserial` installed: start the simulator on the solution folder, then run `python master_dryer.py status`. Before you press start, expect `state` to read `IDLE`, `fault` to read `none` and `material` to read `PLA`. In the simulator these registers may not update, because the FreeRTOS task that publishes them does not start there (see lesson 87). The values above are what a real Blue Pill shows. Compare the temperature with the NTC value on the simulated sensor, and fix any mismatch in your register map.

## Lesson 119: Try it: the bootloader in the simulator

1. Build the starter firmware from the workspace root: `python -I tools/build.py projects/0118-dryer-modbus-bootloader/starter --clean`. The build should finish without errors. Its output folder contains `dryer.map`, the map file this lesson uses.
2. Open the map file and search for `.app_header` and `.app_vectors`. Expect the header at 0x08004000 with size 0x20, and the vector table at 0x08004200 with size 0x130.
3. Open `projects/0118-dryer-modbus-bootloader/starter` in VS Code, press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> to build, then <kbd>F1</kbd> → *Wokwi: Start Simulator*. On the serial monitor, expect `BOOT: checking application slot` followed by `BOOT: image valid, jumping`. The application's own lines follow the jump on a real board. The application runs FreeRTOS, which does not start in the simulator (see lesson 87), so its lines may not appear there. A real board prints `DRYER RTOS OK`, the first line of the solution's `main.c`.
4. Break the header on purpose. In `starter/boot/app_vectors.c`, change the first field of the header initialiser from `APP_IMAGE_MAGIC` to `0u`. Rebuild and start the simulator again. Expect `BOOT: no valid image, staying in the bootloader` and no application output. This change touches only the header, so the bootloader's check is the one that fails.
5. Undo the change, so the magic is `APP_IMAGE_MAGIC` again, and rebuild. The serial monitor should show the jump again.

## Files you work on

- `app/regmap.c` (2 places marked `TODO(learner)`)
- `rtos/tasks.c`

## Done when

The serial monitor prints `DRYER RTOS OK`.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint for the temperature register</summary>

The temperature is in hundredths of a degree. Divide by 10 to get tenths, and store it as an unsigned 16-bit value by casting through a signed 16-bit type. The test for −5.00 °C expects 0xFFCE, which is −50 in two's complement.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint for step 4</summary>

The first field of the header initialiser in `app_vectors.c` is the magic. The bootloader compares it with `APP_IMAGE_MAGIC` in `app_image.h`, and that comparison is the first of its checks. Change only the header, not the define, so the two sides disagree.

</details>
